models.crnn.onnx: 942,166-param CRNN+CTC; the graph DECLARES input [1,1,32,320] and output [1,40,38] (read from the file). The width axis is FIXED at 320 = the training clamp realdata.MAX_W; app/js/recognizer.js serves whatever width the axis declares, see note

note: Exported by `bash run.sh export`; parity verified against PyTorch (max|d| 4.77e-07 restorer, 2.05e-05 crnn at W=320 as exported, 1.29e+00 encoder int8, 8.94e-08 head fp32). THE APP IS WIDTH-ADAPTIVE. app/js/recognizer.js reads the width axis off the session it just loaded (engineWidth()) and takes one of two paths: a NUMBER -> build the tensor and the row stride at that number, right-pad shorter crops, and trim the decode to the crop's true timestep count, exactly as before; a SYMBOLIC axis -> build them at contentWidth and feed every crop at its NATURAL width, padding nothing, and decode all T. onnxruntime-web 1.20.1 exposes NO input-shape metadata (verified: InferenceSession has only handler/run/release/inputNames/outputNames), so the width is read by probing the session at two widths and taking the number ORT names when it refuses a wrong one -- 'Got invalid dimensions for input: input ... index: 3 Got: 63 Expected: 320'. A refused run does not damage the session. VERIFIED IN THE BROWSER (app/tools/dynamic_width_check.js, the app's own module, webkit AND chromium, ort-web 1.20.1 wasm): with artifacts/crnn_dynamic.onnx the app reports engine.width = 'dynamic' and its decode equals the PyTorch reference at W = 32, 47, 63, 64, 128, 200 and 256, with T equal to PyTorch's T at each (which is ceil-like, not floor: 6 at W=47 and 8 at W=63 against floor(W/8) = 5 and 7 -- which is why the natural path must decode all T instead of reusing the trim as a mask); with app/models/crnn.onnx it reports engine.width = 320, the number ORT itself declares for that file, and its padded decode equals an independently built padded-320 reference at the same widths. 320 IS THE TRAINING CLAMP realdata.MAX_W = 320 and it is NOT NEGOTIABLE: it is the crop cap the app passes to cropForRecognizer, crop_to_array clamps every training crop to it, and the corpus median IS that clamp (98.8% of held-out crops exceed 256px). crnn.onnx shipped at 256 for a while on the belief that 256 sat above the median crop -- it sat BELOW it, so the app truncated the tail off ~99% of lines before the model saw them: on 200 held-out crops exact line match was 44.7% at natural width against 0.0% cut to 256, with the read changed on 200 of 200 ('PATIENT JANE DOE DOB 04021979' -> 'PERIENT JANE DOE 2O08010', 'DATE 01102026' -> 'DATE 01020'). TWO CLAIMS THIS NOTE USED TO MAKE WERE WRONG. (1) 'crnn.onnx width is FIXED because aten::lstm cannot export with a dynamic sequence length' -- the LSTM op is not the obstacle. SightLineCRNN.set_export_mode(True) runs an explicit per-timestep Python LSTM loop, and tracing THAT unrolls the recurrence and bakes T into the graph; tracing the FUSED nn.LSTM instead (export mode OFF, with torch.onnx.export(..., dynamo=False), since the dynamo exporter's aten.lstm decomposition rebuilds the same loop) lowers to a real ONNX LSTM op whose sequence axis is dynamic natively. artifacts/crnn_dynamic.onnx is that export: input ['batch', 1, 32, 'width'], output ['batch', 'timesteps', 38], and the exporter's own tolerance check reports max|d| <= 3.2e-05 against eager PyTorch at every width tested, including 47 and 63 where T is not floor(w/8). It is DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: models/ocr/crnn.pt is rewritten every epoch, so the graph must be re-exported from the FINAL checkpoint, and the swap is then a pure file replacement (copy it over app/models/crnn.onnx) -- nothing in the app depends on it having happened, and the fixed-320 path above is still what runs today. (2) That a padded region was self-correcting, because the CTC loss ignores it. The LOSS does ignore a padded region; the MODEL does not -- the two-layer BIDIRECTIONAL LSTM's backward pass starts at the RIGHT EDGE, i.e. inside the padding, so padded zeros move the hidden states across the VALID frames (measured max |delta| 9.10 at content width 64, 15.28 at 200, in logit units). 74.7% of held-out crops are padded at all against the 320 clamp, and isolated to the same weights on the realistic serve distribution the padded path scores crop-level exact 19.0% / CER 0.308 against 30.5% / 0.198 at natural width, agreeing with the natural decode on only 43% of crops. So the fixed path is a known loss to be replaced by the swap, not a neutral default.
